title: Existence of 4-critical graphs on n vertices
statement: For every natural number $n$ with $n = 4$ or $n \ge 6$, there is a simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices that is $4$-critical: its chromatic number is $\chi(G) = 4$, and every proper subgraph $H \subsetneq G$ satisfies $\chi(H) < \chi(G)$.
hypotheses_covered: vertex set has exactly n vertices
replaced:
\emph{For \texttt{n = 4} and all \texttt{n $\ge$ 6},
construct a 4-critical graph on \texttt{n} vertices.}
